MUR · Tractive battery

Balancing for Dummies

How to set the accumulator balancing and babysit it safely. Follow the steps in order. If a step doesn't make sense, open the I'm stuck panel under it.

Elec HV trained only Setup 10 min Needs someone present the whole time

Setup

  1. 1

    Set up the exclusion zone

    Before anything else, close off the battery area with the yellow chains so no one wanders in. It needs a chain on both sides.

    • The chains are in the blue storage tub, with the warning signs.
    • Outside side: clip one end onto the eye bolt on the brick pillar just outside the roller door and run it across the front.
    • Inside side: clip one end onto the hook on the white pillar by the blue storage bins and run it across to the wall on the other side.

    Raining? Don't open the main garage door and skip the outside chain. Just use the inside chain and leave the garage door closed. The door being open isn't essential.

  2. 2

    Grab the Linux laptop

    It lives in the Kincrome tool chest labelled T, second drawer down. If it isn't there, check on top of the charger unit.

  3. 3

    Open the steel fire box

    The big galvanised box (the "bomb proof" box. It isn't, but we like to think it is).

    • Undo the side locks.
    • Push the middle handle in, twist it to the side and lift it up.
    • Lift the whole lid up.
    I'm stuck: show me how to open the box
    1. Undo the side lock on each side of the lid.
    2. Push the black middle handle in towards the box.
    3. Twist it to the side, then lift it up.
    4. Grab the handle at the bottom of the lid and lift the whole lid up.
  4. 4

    Find the battery and charger

    The tractive battery is in front of you inside the box. The charger unit is on the trolley next to it.

  5. 5

    Plug in the battery LV connector

    Grab the tractive battery low voltage connector. Line it up with the socket, then rotate the sleeve clockwise until it clicks and won't spin any further.

  6. 6

    Set up the laptop

    • Plug in the USB-C charger floating around nearby. Do this first, the laptop dies really quickly.
    • Plug the second USB-C cable into the laptop. Its other end goes to the CANdaptor, which plugs into the charger unit.
  7. 7

    Log in and open the CAN ACCY tool

    Turn the laptop on. Password is MUR2026.

    The CAN ACCY TOOL window should already be open. If it isn't, check recent apps.

    I'm stuck: it's not in recent apps

    Open a terminal and run this:

    cd ~/zephyr-workspace/mur-embedded && ./tools/bench/can-accy-tool.sh

    The first run can take a minute while it sets itself up. If the window never appears, the terminal shows why. Screenshot it and send it to the group chat.

  8. 8

    Two vital checks

    You shouldn't need to touch anything here, just confirm it looks like this.

    A. Red battery key is ON

    It's the left switch on the charger panel. This powers the tractive battery fans.

    B. Only one side of fans plugged in

    Driver's left plugged in. Driver's right unplugged.

  9. 9

    Turn the mains on at the wall

    Flip the wall isolator to ON. Balancing should start straight away.

  10. 10
    Really important

    Listen for the fans within 10 seconds

    About 10 seconds after the mains goes on, you should hear some loud fans kick in.

    No fans? Turn the mains off at the wall straight away.

    The fans are what keep the BMS cool. Without them it very easily gets up to 150°C. We found this out the hard way.

  11. 11

    Connect and enable balancing

    • Top left of the tool, hit Refresh next to Port. The port should fill in with something like /dev/ttyUSB2. Then hit Connect. Pack voltage and cell voltages should fill in.
    • Top right, hit Balance… to open the Balancing popup.
    • In the popup, tick Forced balancing, then hit Send. Leave Start voltage and Mismatch as they are unless the HV team says otherwise.

    Every time the accy is power cycled (mains off at the wall, or the LV connector unplugged), balancing turns off. Tick Forced balancing and hit Send again.

    Check it's working: orange squares in the cell grid in the popup are cells being balanced. The line above should say BMS balancing · active. The grid only shows cells 1 to 56. Cells 57 to 108 always show as unknown, which is normal.

    I'm stuck: it won't connect

    If you see a red CANdaptor connection lost message, the tool can't talk to the battery.

    1. Check the CANdaptor is plugged in properly at both ends (step 6).
    2. Check the power is on at the wall (step 9).
    3. Unplug the CANdaptor's USB cable from the laptop and plug it back in.
    4. Hit Refresh, then Connect again. If the Port box stays empty after Refresh, the laptop can't see the CANdaptor, so go back to 1.
    I'm stuck: no orange squares
    1. Make sure you ticked Forced balancing and hit Send.
    2. Has the accy been power cycled since? Balancing turns off every time. Tick and Send again.
    3. A cell only balances when it's above the Start voltage and more than the Mismatch (10 mV) above the lowest cell. Near the end of a balance, few or no squares light up.
    4. Grey cells on the main chart mean the tool has no fresh reading for them. If most are grey, it's a connection problem: see "it won't connect" above.

While it's running

This is why it needs babysitting. The slaves are known to get hot when balancing. Nothing should happen, but someone needs to be there if it does. Everything below is in the CAN ACCY tool.

Keep an eye on BMS temps

Top right, under Temperatures. Anything over 60°C means stop.

Max cell / Master
Every 3 to 4 hours Post cell volts

Send them to the tracker straight from the CAN ACCY tool. Three clicks, steps below.

  1. Add a note if you want, then hit Add cell voltages to Liam's balance tracker under the Notes box. It only works while the tool is connected.
  2. A browser notification pops up saying the new issue page is ready. Click the notification to open it.
  3. On the GitHub page the numbers are already filled in. Hit the green Create button. You need to be signed in to GitHub. It shows on the Tracking tab within a couple of minutes.

Hot or smoking? Stop.

  1. Turn the power off at the wall, ASAP.
  2. Unplug the accy (the LV connector).
  3. Close the fire box lid.

Then tell the Elec HV group chat what happened.

Packing up

Run the setup in reverse.

  1. Power off at the wall.
  2. Unplug the LV connector, then both USB-C cables from the laptop.
  3. Put the laptop back in chest T, second drawer down.
  4. Close the fire box lid, put the middle handle back down and do up the side locks.
  5. Take down both chains and put them back in the blue tub.

Still stuck?

Something not matching the photos, won't connect, or you're just not sure? Don't guess with the battery. Stop where you are and message the group.

Message the Elec HV group chat

Assumptions

Changes here are saved on this device only.

State of charge comes from a Sony/Murata VTC6 curve built from ENEPAQ's 1C discharge test, shifted up 75 mV to estimate the resting voltage. Groups are 7 × 3 Ah = 21 Ah. The 75 mV shift is an estimate, so treat the absolute SOC figures as roughly ±5%. Against real balancing data from 2 to 3 November the curve predicted the high cell to within about 6 mV over a day. The Balanced percentage compares readings against each other and is much less sensitive to the curve. Time left is worked out from the bleed resistor alone: the high group is stepped down the voltage curve to the low cell's state of charge, and at each step the bleed current is that cell voltage divided by the resistor, times the duty cycle.

Voltage to SOC table

Sony/Murata VTC6 rest-voltage curve (from ENEPAQ's 1C discharge test, +75 mV) used for every SOC figure on this page. Voltages between rows are interpolated linearly; at or below the first row reads 0% and above the last reads 100%.
